assigned.title: CI executes every script suite the repository declares, and a failing validate job says something
assigned.acceptance:
CREATED ON gpt-architect's ROUND-107 DIRECTIVE. Two defects, one file.

A. EVERY SUITE THE REPOSITORY DECLARES IS EXECUTED BY CI. The validate job mirrors `npm run test:scripts` as separate named steps, and its own comment says 'a FIFTH script added to it must be added here too' -- and then records that the drift it warns about had already happened once. It has happened twice more: `test:scripts` now names SIX scripts and this job runs FOUR of them. `scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs` and `node --test scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs` (30 cases) are in the alias and in no step. `apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs` (17 cases) is in no alias and no step and is run by nothing at all.
REQUIRED: all three execute in CI and fail the build when they fail.
REQUIRED: the mirror is kept in step BY A MECHANISM, not by a comment asking a human to remember. A note that a hand-kept list must be kept in step is already in the file, it did not keep the list in step, and a fourth occurrence of the same drift is not a thing to apologise for again.
REQUIRED: the added suites run where their dependencies allow. The six pre-install steps are pre-install on purpose -- they use Node builtins only, so a dependency failure cannot mask a control-plane or structure failure -- and a suite placed there must actually hold to that.
REQUIRED, and quoted from the directive: 'do not turn apps/desktop into a workspace if that causes validators to traverse generated packaging output'. Round 106 measured exactly that and it does: a dependency-free apps/desktop/package.json costs 8 lockfile lines and turbo picks the suite up, but `validate-workspace-deps.mjs` then walks apps/desktop/sidecar/server/ -- generated packaging output carrying its own .gitignore of '*' -- and demands the manifest declare `next`. The measurement is in coordination/WINDOWS_LIFECYCLE_WIRING.md section 8.

B. A FAILING `validate` JOB SAYS SOMETHING ACTIONABLE. On run 37028642916 at 30cef6e the job aborted at 10m 38s with one annotation, 'Process completed with exit code 134', naming no step -- having PASSED at 25m 4s and 27m 29s on the two runs before it. Exit 134 is SIGABRT. The engineering session cannot read run logs or download artifacts (the Actions API answers 403) and so could not determine which step aborted, let alone why; two local reproductions of the prime suspect passed, at 1261s ambient and 1807s under a runner-like heap cap.
REQUIRED: a run page carries enough to tell a reader WHICH step aborted and under what machine conditions -- at minimum core count, total and available memory, free disk, the Node version and NODE_OPTIONS -- without needing the log or the artifact.
REQUIRED, and quoted from the directive: 'DO NOT declare OOM. DO NOT increase memory merely because exit 134 occurred. DO NOT increase timeouts without evidence. DO NOT add retries to hide it. Improve diagnostics first.' Nothing in this task may change what CI runs or how much it is given. Diagnostics only.
REQUIRED, and quoted from the directive: no secret leakage. Nothing added here may print the environment wholesale, a token, or a value this repository has not already published; an allowlist of named variables, never a dump.

C. THE JOB'S COST DOES NOT GROW MATERIALLY. The three added suites take under a second between them locally. Diagnostics must stay cheap enough that nobody is tempted to remove them the next time the job is slow.
assigned.notes:
CREATED IN ROUND 107 on the commander's relay of gpt-architect's directive, which named the task id, the write surface and the review dependencies. THE ACCEPTANCE TEXT ABOVE IS CLAUDE'S RENDERING of the requirements in that directive, not a transcription of it -- the two passages in quotation marks are verbatim and everything else is Claude's wording of what the directive asked for. Correct it in review if the rendering is wider or narrower than intended.

THE LANE IS A CHOICE AND IT IS DECLARED RATHER THAN BURIED. Two candidate lanes were considered.
  - INFRA is the obvious reading of 'CI workflow' and it is where PW-0501 sat, because PW-0501's subject was producing a Windows build artifact.
  - INTEGRATION is what was chosen. The subject here is not a pipeline capability: it is that components which already exist -- three test suites, all passing, all committed -- are not connected to the build graph, and that a job's failure is not legible to the people who have to act on it. That is wiring, and this repository has never treated .github/workflows/ as Infra-exclusive: PL-AI-0003 added the dispatcher step to this same file under lane Coordination, and PL-0704 and PW-0312 both wrote ci.yml under lane Frontend. Lane has followed subject matter here, not file path.
THE CONFOUND, STATED BECAUSE IT IS REAL: claude-infra is at maxParallel 1 and the slot is held by PW-0208 in REVIEW, so Integration is also the lane with capacity. Round 105 forbade re-laning a task to obtain an idle agent and that prohibition is respected on its own terms -- nothing was moved -- but a new task's lane chosen while one candidate is busy deserves the disclosure rather than the silence. Re-lane it to Infra in review if the reasoning above does not hold; nothing in the implementation depends on the lane.

CONFLICTS, CHECKED IN BOTH FIELDS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS BEFORE CREATION. .github/workflows/ci.yml: written by PL-0001, PL-0704, PL-AI-0002 and PW-0312, all DONE; read by PL-AI-0003, PW-0102, PW-0501 and PL-0406, all DONE. No open task holds it in either field. package.json is in PW-0503's allowedPaths (READY, unowned) -- holding it here as a READ-ONLY reviewDependency reserves nothing, and the cost is recorded: if PW-0503 is later claimed and writes package.json, it stales any approval of this task computed before that write. scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs is under PW-0502's and PW-0503's allowedPaths (both READY, unowned), again read-only here. apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs is under PW-0208's allowedPaths and PW-0208 IS ACTIVE, in REVIEW -- so this task must not write it, and it does not: it is a reviewDependency. The reverse direction matters more and is clear: this task's only write is ci.yml, which PW-0208 names in neither field, so claiming this cannot stale PW-0208's pending review.

WHY THE ORPHANED-SUITE HALF IS NOT SOLVED BY MAKING apps/desktop A WORKSPACE: measured in round 106 and reverted. See acceptance clause A.

typecheck.evidence: npm run typecheck: 22 tasks successful, 22 total. STATED PLAINLY: no TypeScript project compiles .github/workflows/ci.yml, so this records that nothing else was disturbed and nothing about the change. The evidence that bears on the change is under the unit gate.

unit.evidence:
RE-RECORDED to add the end-to-end execution of the alias this task wires, which the first recording could not carry because the run was still in flight.

npm run test:scripts: EXIT 0, 2229 SECONDS, tree quiescent, NODE_OPTIONS=--report-on-fatalerror and without this container's usual 8 GB heap. All six suites green -- test-validate-env 38 scenarios, test-ai-control-plane 73, test-validate-repo 20 assertion groups plus the 27 workspace-deps and 21 turbo-graph groups delegated from it, TEST-DESKTOP-TARGET 9 ASSERTIONS and WINDOWS/TEST-LIFECYCLE 30 PASS 0 FAIL -- the last two being exactly the suites this task adds to CI, executed here as part of the alias the new mirror check now enforces. cloud/test-dispatcher 35 scenarios. No temp roots left behind.

A DURATION TREND WORTH THE REVIEWER'S ATTENTION, recorded in full as a ci.run_observed event this round: the same suite measured 1261 s and 1807 s in rounds 104 and 106 and is now 2229 s. It spawns a fresh node per scenario and every one parses the whole 1.5 MB control/tasks.json, so its runtime scales with the size of the board. That does NOT explain exit 134 and is not offered as one -- validate passed at 25m and 27m and aborted at 10.5m, and a growth trend predicts the opposite of that -- but it is the context the next person needs.

THE EARLIER RUN TODAY EXITED 1 AT 2090 s on the suite's own guard, "running the test suite must not mutate the real control/tasks.json". That was my doing: I edited tasks.json four times while a suite that copies the repository was running. Recorded as an operator error rather than left to look like a defect. Everything above is the clean re-run.

EVERYTHING IN THE PREVIOUS RECORDING STANDS UNCHANGED: the three newly-wired suites, the mirror check proved by its failures including against the ci.yml at HEAD, the diagnostics executed under GitHub's own shell flags, --report-on-fatalerror verified end to end, and the secret-leakage test in which a value present once in the raw V8 report appears zero times in the rendered summary.

assigned.title: The product-readiness instrument is out of date, and it is the figure the commander reads
assigned.acceptance:
FOUND BY THE ROUND-107 PROJECT-WIDE GAP HUNT. control/product-readiness.json answers the question the engineering board deliberately does not -- 'can a person install this on a Windows PC and watch something' -- and its own header says it must never be confused with the task count. It is the honest instrument, and it has gone stale in the direction that makes the product look worse than it is. Several items state as FACT things that stopped being true rounds ago, and cite line numbers and absences as evidence.

DEMONSTRABLY FALSE ITEMS, each checkable in one command. (a) packagingRelease.windows-build 'absent -- Every CI job is ubuntu-latest; no windows-latest runner exists': .github/workflows/windows.yml and desktop-shell-ci.yml both run on windows-latest and both SUCCEEDED on 2c037d5. (b) packagingRelease.installer 'absent -- No NSIS, WiX, MSI, MSIX or Inno configuration anywhere': the Windows job produces exactly one MSI and one NSIS installer every run, asserts the inventory with digests, installs the MSI, verifies the installed tree and uninstalls it; the artifact is 71.3 MB. (c) packagingRelease.app-identity 'absent -- No product name, publisher, icons, version scheme or app-data location': tauri.conf.json declares productName and identifier and sidecar.rs declares the data, cache and log locations, which scripts/windows/installed-identity.mjs derives from. (d) windowsDesktop.tauri-shell 'absent -- no binary can be produced': one is produced and installed on every Windows run. (e) nativePlayback.capability-routing 'absent -- design-only': adapter-routing.ts shipped with PW-0203. (f) nativePlayback.track-selection 'absent -- zero getTextTracks/selectAudioLanguage callers': web-player-adapter.ts calls both. (g) productUi.offline-network-state 'absent -- No navigator.onLine, no offline banner, no retry-on-reconnect': PW-0309 shipped all three with browser coverage. (h) testingReliability.windows-e2e 'absent -- No test has ever run on Windows': 25 Rust tests run on windows-latest every push. (i) several notes describe PW-0102, PW-0303, PW-0312 and PW-0403 as in REVIEW or pending; all are DONE.

REQUIRED: every item is re-scored against the tree and the notes rewritten to what is now true, with the same evidence discipline the file already demands -- a file path, a workflow, or a run.
REQUIRED: the scoring rules in the header are APPLIED, not relaxed. 'present' still means implemented AND REACHABLE BY A USER OF THE SHIPPED APP. An installer CI produces that nobody has launched is not 'present' for a user; several of the items above move to partial rather than to present, and saying so is the point of the exercise.
REQUIRED: the direction of each correction is stated. A figure that goes UP because the product improved and a figure that goes up because the instrument was wrong are different events, and conflating them would make the next reading untrustworthy too.
REQUIRED: engineeringFoundation.rate-limits is re-stated precisely rather than flipped. 'No rate limit on any route' is false for the AUTH routes -- better-auth 1.7.5's default rate limiting is enabled whenever the server is in production and applies 3-per-10-seconds to anything under /sign-in and /sign-up -- and true for the application's own routes. The distinction is not pedantry: PL-0715 is very likely a consequence of the half that exists, and docs/SECURITY.md residual risk R2 is cited as the evidence for a claim that is now half wrong.
REQUIRED: coordination/PRODUCT_READINESS.md is regenerated by scripts/product-readiness.mjs rather than edited, which that file says in its own header.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing the scoring rules, the weights, or the dimension list. Those are gpt-architect's and the commander's; this task corrects facts, not the instrument.
assigned.notes:
CREATED IN ROUND 107 by the project-wide gap hunt the directive asked for. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A TIDY-UP: this is the number that answers 'how far is the product', and it currently reports packagingRelease at 0% on a tree where CI builds, installs, verifies and uninstalls a real Windows installer on every push. Under-reporting is not the safe direction -- it hides which dimensions are genuinely stuck (realContent at 10%, blocked on a licensed provider; nativePlayback, blocked behind PW-0103 on the commander's hardware) behind dimensions that only look stuck.

NOBODY OWNED THE FILE. control/** and coordination/** belong to PL-0002, PL-AI-0001 and PL-AI-0002, all DONE -- the same shape as the windows.yml problem reported in round 105 and resolved in round 107. Conflict-checked in both fields in both directions at filing: no task in any state declares control/product-readiness.json or coordination/PRODUCT_READINESS.md specifically, and the active tasks are PW-0208 (REVIEW), PW-0602 (IN_PROGRESS), PL-0714 (REVIEW), PW-0206 (REVIEW) and PW-0307 (IN_PROGRESS), none of which names either path.

control/tasks.json is a reviewDependency and NOT a write surface: this task reads task states to check its own claims and must not edit them.

unit.evidence:
THE GATE IS "unit" BECAUSE THAT IS WHAT THE TASK DECLARES, AND IT IS THE WEAKER HALF OF THE EVIDENCE. node scripts/product-readiness.mjs regenerates coordination/PRODUCT_READINESS.md from the data and exits 0; node scripts/ai-control-plane.mjs validate passes at 118 tasks; npm run repo:validate passes. The document was REGENERATED and not edited, which its own header requires.

THE EVIDENCE THAT MATTERS IS THAT EVERY CORRECTION WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE TREE OR AGAINST A RUN, one at a time.
  windows-build: runs 37036128017 (windows.yml, 5m 0s) and 37036127979 (desktop-shell-ci.yml, 2m 25s), both SUCCESS at 2c037d5, both windows-latest. The old note cited three ci.yml line numbers as proof that no Windows runner existed.
  installer: the Windows job asserts exactly one MSI and one NSIS bundle with SHA-256 digests, installs the MSI silently, verifies the installed tree and uninstalls it; the uploaded artifact is 71.3 MB.
  app-identity: tauri.conf.json read -- productName "Project Liberty", publisher "Project Liberty", identifier app.projectliberty.desktop, four icons. PARTIAL and not present, because the fifth thing the old note named is genuinely missing: tauri.conf.json states NO version, the bundle inherits Cargo.toml 0.1.0, and nothing decides the next number. That is the rule being applied rather than a flip.
  capability-routing: adapter-routing.ts and its suite exist (PW-0203).
  track-selection: web-player-adapter.ts calls getTextTracks and selectAudioLanguage; the claim of "zero callers" is false by grep.
  offline-network-state: network-state.ts, reachability-store.ts, degraded-banner.tsx and degraded-states.spec.ts all exist (PW-0309).
  watchlist-ui, continue-watching, artwork: apps/web/src/app/watchlist/page.tsx, components/continue-watching/continue-watching-rail.tsx imported by app/page.tsx, components/artwork and packages/contracts/src/shared/artwork.ts.
  rate-limits: read out of the installed library rather than assumed -- better-auth 1.7.5 dist/context/create-context.mjs line 172 is `enabled: options.rateLimit?.enabled ?? isProduction`, and dist/api/rate-limiter/index.mjs getDefaultSpecialRules applies window 10 / max 3 to any path starting /sign-in or /sign-up. packages/auth/src/better-auth.ts passes no rateLimit option.
  crash-diagnostics: LOG_RELATIVE_PATH exists in sidecar.rs, so the old note is imprecise -- AND THE SCORE DOES NOT MOVE, because nothing has been observed writing to it. Correcting a note is not the same as raising a score.
  auth-seam and profiles-ui: each kept PARTIAL on the one ground that survived -- noMailTransport throws, and profile avatars are still an initial and a hue -- with the two stale grounds in each corrected.

THREE THINGS I DID NOT DO. The rules, the weights and the dimension list are untouched; they are gpt-architects and the commanders. No item moved to "present" that a user cannot reach -- the Tauri shell stays PARTIAL on an installer CI builds and nobody has launched, and the whole adapter boundary stays partial because player-surface.tsx still drives the controller directly. And the file now states, in its own preamble, that the 46 to 60 move is almost entirely the instrument catching up rather than progress made this round.

NOT VERIFIED: nobody re-derived the weighted arithmetic by hand; it is the renderer the file has always used. And the "reachable by a user" test is applied to the WEB application, as this file has always applied it -- under the strictest reading, where the shipped app is a Windows desktop application nobody has launched, every row would be partial, which is not the question the instrument was built to answer.
